question: I1-D
prompt:
I'm a researcher in the FIESTA Astronomy community (part of the 'FAIR Image Data Workflows in Galaxy' community). Which file format should I use for my image datasets?

Answer briefly. On the last line write exactly one of:
COMMUNITY_CHOICE: <the resource(s) my community has agreed on, comma-separated>
COMMUNITY_CHOICE: NOT_DECLARED   (my community has explicitly not agreed on one)
COMMUNITY_CHOICE: DONT_KNOW      (you cannot tell what my community agreed)
answer:
FITS is the usual format for astronomical image data. It's an IAU-endorsed standard, it keeps metadata in its headers, and Galaxy and most astronomy tools support it well. Many imaging workflows also convert to OME-TIFF or OME-Zarr when they need to work with general bioimage tools.

I don't have a record of what the FIESTA Astronomy community formally agreed in its FAIR Implementation Profile, and I couldn't look it up from here. So FITS is a sensible default, not a confirmed community decision. Check your community's FIP on the FIP Wizard or FAIR Connect to see what it actually declared.

COMMUNITY_CHOICE: DONT_KNOW
